newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee nudges up ahead of U.S. stock news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee nudges up ahead of U.S. stock news.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures closed higher on Friday on keen buying interest and inspired by New York amid hopes of bullish U.S. stock data due later in the day.
The New York market was buoyed by speculative buying on expectations the U.S. Green Coffee Association's (GCA) October stock data would show a drop of between 200,000 to 300,000 60-kg bags.
One trader said the fall was likely to be on the higher side of the range. "Certainly there will be big drawdown," he said. "It's a situation of buying on rumours and sell on facts."
London's benchmark January futures were $10 higher on the day to end at $1,442 a tonne. It had raced to a high of $1,449 but encountered stiff resistance at $1,450.
The second-position contract fell early to a session low of $1,425 on origin selling but recovered later on good roaster buying support. Expiring November was $2 off at $1,501.
Volume on the exchange reached a modest 2,514 lots, centred on the January position.
Structure trading was quiet but activity on the options pit picked up dramatically.
News of a small drop in London's October certified coffee stocks to 1,410 five-tonne-lots was within trade expectation and was viewed as neutral.
The market's attention continued to focus on the U.S. data.
Supplies of green coffee in U.S. warehouses fell in September by 205,000 bags to 1.61 million, the lowest since the GCA began tracking inventories in January, 1988.
New York's December premium to March remained at a large 9.00 U.S. cents a lb reflecting the continued tightness in nearby availabilty.
Tuesday is the first notice day for the December contract. Deceember's open interest stood at 4,461 lots as at the close of business on Thursday, down 1,129 lots from a year earlier.
But certified stocks at U.S. warehouses were virtually nil while coffee pending grading remained relatively small.
"It's largely the question of when coffee is going to come in, there are no stocks and people can hang on for longer than first notice day," said one.
Traders said that shippers would still have time to get their coffee in before the December contract expires next month.
In options, some 1,575 lots changed hands in brisk Friday trade. Volume was swelled by volatility trades to match an early buying interes on March $1,350 puts.
"Today was the busiest day on coffee for quite a while," said one.
